data.title: Fiera Capital Earnings Call Highlights Debt and Outflows
data.description:
Fiera Capital A ((TSE:FSZ)) has held its Q3 earnings call. Read on for the main highlights of the call.

Fiera Capital’s earnings call struck a largely negative tone despite signs of progress. Lower expenses, debt repayment, stronger recent Canadian equity results and resilient existing-client demand were outweighed by major AUM outflows, weaker revenue and performance fees, lower year-over-year EBITDA, elevated leverage and the end of the quarterly dividend.

Balance Sheet Deleveraging

Net debt ended the quarter at $689 million, down $34 million sequentially, as Fiera used stronger free cash flow to repay its credit facility. The funded debt ratio improved to 3.1x from 3.3x in the prior quarter.

More Capacity for Debt Reduction

Management said ending the quarterly dividend will create more than $45 million a year for debt reduction. The retained capital should also support reinvestment in the business and selected growth opportunities.

Broader Investment Platform

Fiera is adding core and quantitative investment strategies to expand the solutions available to clients. Management said the expansion is intended to preserve the firm’s high-conviction investment approach while broadening product choice.

Canadian Equity Team Rebuilt

The Canadian large-cap equity team added three hires with a combined 68 years of experience, including Charles Nadim as head of Canadian equities. Fiera has engaged consultants and clients, retained all but one consultant rating and reported no identified additional outflow pipeline.

Canadian Equity Performance Rebounds

The Canadian Equity Fund gained almost seven percentage points against its index in six weeks, while Canadian Equity Core was about six points ahead year to date. In October, Canadian equity strategies outperformed their benchmark by more than 500 basis points, recovering much of their earlier shortfall.

Wider Equity Momentum

Most flagship equity strategies beat their benchmarks in October, with other Canadian, U.S. and international strategies outperforming by more than 300 basis points. U.S. large-cap growth and U.S. SMID-cap growth ranked in the first or second quartile, while Atlas Group and Frontier markets also added value.

More Stable Sub-Advised Base

Sub-advised assets now represent 16% of total AUM, down from 27% two years ago. Less than one-quarter of the remaining assets are tied to clients with mandates above $1 billion, and management described the base as more stable and largely multi-strategy.

Private Markets Deployment

Fiera deployed nearly $400 million into new private-market projects during the quarter, taking year-to-date deployment to $1.2 billion. Undeployed capital in the pipeline remained substantial at $1.6 billion.

Private Markets Deliver Positive Returns

All private-market strategies generated positive absolute returns during the quarter. Since inception, core and small-cap industrial real estate strategies produced annualized returns of 8% and 13%, while the Direct Lending Opportunities Fund generated a 2.4% quarterly internal rate of return and 12% since inception.

Private Credit Becomes a Priority

Management identified private credit as an important growth area and strategic initiative. Fiera appointed Amit Gupta as global head of real estate debt and added a head of private credit to give the business greater leadership focus.

Strong Demand from Existing Canadian Clients

Core Canadian gross sales totaled $2.1 billion, including about $200 million of new mandates and a $1.9 billion positive net contribution from existing clients. Gross sales were broadly consistent with the previous two quarters.

Fixed Income Holds Long-Term Advantage

Canadian fixed-income strategies had a difficult quarter but finished close to their benchmarks. About 78% of fixed-income AUM outperformed over one year, while 94% outperformed over three years.

Sequential Expense Improvement

SG&A and other expenses excluding share-based compensation fell to $107.4 million, down $5.7 million, or 5%, from the prior quarter. Lower compensation costs led the decline, with travel, marketing and sub-advisory expenses also moving lower.

Cost Savings Build Through the Year

Year-to-date SG&A excluding share-based compensation declined $22.4 million, or 6%. About 70% of the reduction came from lower compensation costs tied to optimization efforts, with the remainder mainly reflecting lower sub-advisory fees.

Adjusted EBITDA Improves Sequentially

Adjusted EBITDA rose to $42.9 million, up $900,000, or 2.1%, from the prior quarter. The adjusted EBITDA margin increased to 28.5% from 27.1%, a 140-basis-point improvement.

Quarterly Net Earnings Increase

Net earnings attributable to shareholders rose to $6.7 million, or $0.06 per basic and diluted share. That compared with $3.5 million, or $0.03 per share, in the prior quarter.

Free Cash Flow Remains Resilient

Last-12-month free cash flow was $90 million, down $3 million sequentially but up $3 million from the same period last year. Lower lease payments and interest expense helped offset higher dividends paid to noncontrolling interests.

Directly Managed Fees Hold Steady

Base management fees from directly managed mandates were broadly unchanged from the previous quarter and flat year over year. Adjusted basic earnings per share also remained unchanged year over year at $0.23.

Operations and Technology Upgrade

Fiera continues to optimize operations, replace legacy platforms and develop artificial intelligence initiatives. The company said these efforts are designed to improve efficiency and employee productivity.

Distribution and Talent Focus

Fiera appointed Emerson Savage as head of U.S. distribution and co-head of distribution in Canada. The company is concentrating distribution resources on markets and strategies with the strongest demand, while increasing engagement with existing clients and seeking investment talent.

AUM Falls on Outflows and Markets

Total assets under management ended the quarter at $151.4 billion, down 7.4% sequentially. The decline reflected $8.3 billion of net outflows and a $3.5 billion adverse market impact, largely caused by rising rates in fixed income.

Public Markets Face Heavy Pressure

Public-markets AUM fell 8.4%, including $5.2 billion of sub-advised outflows and $2.5 billion from directly managed assets. The directly managed decline was concentrated in Canadian large-cap equity mandates.

Sub-Advised Mandates Lose Assets

Sub-advised net outflows of $5.2 billion included $3 billion of client rebalancing in the U.S. and Asia and $2.2 billion of lost mandates. About $1.5 billion of the lost mandates had been announced previously and transferred directly to PineStone.

Canadian Large-Cap Attrition Concentrated in Newer Accounts

Canadian large-cap outflows were concentrated among newer relationships, with about half of the attrition coming from clients whose average strategy tenure was 1.5 years. The business retained $15 billion of AUM, and more than 85% was held by clients with relationships exceeding five years.

Private Markets AUM Also Declines

Private-markets AUM decreased about $400 million, or 1.8%. Nearly $200 million of new mandates was more than offset by returned capital and the loss of $300 million of undeployed capital after a client chose to manage a U.K. real estate mandate internally.

Revenue Moves Lower

Third-quarter revenue was $150 million, down 3% from the prior quarter and 10% from the same quarter last year. Year-to-date revenue fell 7%, mainly because of lower sub-advised base fees, weaker performance fees and a lower share of joint-venture and associate earnings.

Performance Fees Contract Sharply

Performance fees were $600,000, compared with $2.1 million in the prior quarter and $7 million a year earlier. Year-to-date performance fees totaled $2.7 million, down from $9.7 million, with most of the decline linked to the Global Agriculture Fund.

Public-Market Base Fees Decline

Public-markets base management fees fell 5% sequentially to $91 million. They were down 11% year over year and 7% year to date, reflecting lower average AUM, reduced fee rates and a shift toward sub-advised strategies.

Commitment and Transaction Fees Fall

Commitment and transaction fees were $3.1 million, down from $3.7 million in the prior quarter. Year-to-date fees reached $8.1 million, compared with $9.7 million in the prior-year period.

Joint-Venture Earnings Weaken

Year-to-date earnings from joint ventures and associates declined to $3.7 million from $6 million a year earlier. Quarterly earnings were $2.6 million, although that represented a $200,000 sequential increase.

EBITDA Down Year Over Year

Adjusted EBITDA declined $7.4 million, or 15%, from the same quarter last year. Year-to-date adjusted EBITDA was $127.7 million, down from $139.4 million, with lower performance fees accounting for about five percentage points of the reduction.

Adjusted Earnings Per Share Declines

Adjusted net earnings fell $1.1 million year over year to $23.9 million. Fully diluted adjusted earnings per share declined to $0.19 from $0.23 a year earlier, partly reflecting dilution from the 7.4% hybrid debentures issued in May 2026.

Leverage Remains Elevated

The net debt ratio stayed at 3.8x because lower net debt was offset by lower last-12-month adjusted EBITDA. The ratio was up 0.3x from the third quarter last year, while the funded debt ratio rose to 3.1x from 2.9x.

Quarterly Dividend Discontinued

Management recommended, and the Board approved, ending the quarterly dividend. The decision is intended to retain capital, reduce leverage and improve balance-sheet flexibility, but it also removes an important source of shareholder income.

Equity Markets Remain Challenging

Quality-focused equity strategies faced elevated volatility and narrow market leadership during the quarter. Gains were concentrated in commodity-linked shares and mega-cap technology companies, producing mixed absolute and relative results across Fiera’s equity platform.

Canadian Equity Hit by Materials Underweight

Canadian equity performance was hurt by Fiera’s underweight position in materials. Gold and silver miners rallied during the period, creating a headwind for the firm’s relative returns.

Fixed Income Faces Rate Volatility

Fixed-income results were pressured by rising interest rates and uncertainty over central-bank policy. Despite the difficult quarter, longer-term relative performance remained positive across the Canadian fixed-income platform.

New-Client Sales Under Pressure

Fiera reported near-term pressure on new-client sales, especially outside Canada. The company is adjusting its local presence and distribution resources toward markets and strategies where demand is strongest.

Limited Visibility on Performance Fees

Management declined to provide fourth-quarter performance-fee guidance because markets have been volatile. Executives pointed to the sharp market movements of the previous 60 days as a reason for limited visibility.

Forward-Looking Guidance

Debt reduction is management’s first priority, with the dividend change expected to provide more than $45 million a year for repayment and another meaningful reduction by this time next year. The current expense run rate is considered a reasonable basis for the fourth quarter, while performance fees remain unpredictable and direct transfers in 2026 are expected to be lower than in 2025.

Fiera also said it does not expect the same level of leakage to PineStone and sees less of an outflow pipeline in sub-advised strategies. Management reported no additional Canadian-equity outflow pipeline, while cost optimization remains an ongoing effort.

Fiera Capital delivered some encouraging operational gains, including lower expenses, better recent equity performance and continued private-markets activity. However, the quarter was defined by shrinking AUM, falling revenue and EBITDA, high leverage and a suspended dividend, leaving investors focused on whether debt reduction and business investments can restore durable growth.

Record Quarter Supports Strong Annual Performance

Dexterra reported revenue of CAD 291 million in the quarter, up from CAD 281 million a year earlier, while adjusted EBITDA rose 9% to CAD 38 million. The adjusted EBITDA margin improved to 13% from 12.5%, and adjusted earnings per share increased 12% to CAD 0.28 as management described the period as traditionally its strongest quarter.

Growth Broad-Based Despite Wildfire Weakness

Revenue growth came from strong workforce accommodation occupancy, rental activity, organic gains and the Right Choice acquisition. Those gains offset significantly lower wildfire support and workforce accommodation installation and demobilization activity compared with last year, when those services provided a larger contribution.

Market Value Reaches a New Milestone

Dexterra surpassed CAD 1 billion in market capitalization for the first time in its history. Management linked the milestone to progress in facilities management, workforce accommodations and strategic acquisitions, supported by disciplined capital allocation and consistent financial performance.

Support Services Deliver Margin Expansion

Support Services revenue increased 8% to CAD 253 million, driven by workforce accommodation occupancy, U.S. facilities management growth and the Right Choice acquisition. Organic growth reached 4.5%, adjusted EBITDA climbed 18% to CAD 29 million, and the margin expanded to 11.5% from 10.5%, with both major platforms recording mid-single-digit organic growth.

Occupancy and Inflation Management Lift Profitability

Higher-margin workforce accommodation contracts helped improve Support Services profitability, with the margin excluding PVC rising to 11% from 10%. Management said supply-chain initiatives, contractual inflation provisions and pricing adjustments were containing cost pressures, while direct costs represented a smaller share of revenue in both segments.

PVC Investment Advances Its Platform

Dexterra’s 40% PVC investment contributed CAD 1.3 million to adjusted EBITDA, up from CAD 0.9 million a year earlier. The partnership is modernizing its proprietary PVC Connect facility-management software on time and on budget, while building the structure needed to support PVC’s distributed U.S. model.

Asset-Based Services Improve Mix

Asset Based Services generated CAD 39 million in revenue, with higher-margin rental revenue rising 2.3% on strong equipment utilization, solid access matting activity and the Right Choice contribution. Adjusted EBITDA was CAD 16 million, but the margin increased sharply to 41% from 34% because of the favorable shift toward rental revenue.

Cash Flow and Leverage Strengthen

Dexterra generated CAD 38 million of free cash flow in the quarter and CAD 61 million year to date, helped by profitability and improved working capital. Net debt fell to CAD 193 million from CAD 206 million in the second quarter, while net debt to adjusted EBITDA improved to 1.4 times from 1.6 times at the end of 2025.

Returns and Capital Discipline Remain in Focus

Trailing 12-month return on equity reached 15.4%, exceeding Dexterra’s 15% target. The company spent CAD 15 million on capital expenditures, including CAD 12 million to refurbish about 500 workforce accommodation beds, an investment management described as targeted, cost-effective and capable of generating attractive returns.

Liquidity Supports Growth and Shareholder Returns

Dexterra’s CAD 425 million credit facility runs to 2029 and has significant unused capacity, along with an uncommitted CAD 150 million accordion. The company repurchased about 118,000 shares during the quarter under its normal course issuer bid, which permits purchases of up to 3 million shares, and declared a CAD 0.10 per-share dividend payable January 15, 2027.

Pipeline Spans Canada and the United States

Management described the sales pipeline as strong and diverse across mining, energy, infrastructure, government, defense, workforce accommodations and remote facilities management. Dexterra has strengthened its U.S. leadership and sales organization supporting PVC, CMI and self-perform integrated facilities management, with new project traction in both Canada and the U.S.

New Contracts and Indigenous Partnerships Expand Reach

The company secured new facilities-management and integrated facilities-management wins in 2026, including contracts within PVC. Dexterra is also pursuing nation-building opportunities in areas such as pipelines, power, roads, defense and data centers, drawing on more than 80 Indigenous community partnerships and its national operating presence.

Fleet Expansion Targets Remote Demand

Dexterra has about 2,500 fleet beds available for medium-term deployment and is pursuing another 1,500 beds. Together, those additions would increase deployable capacity by 4,000 beds and raise total fleet capacity to 14,000, with acquisitions expected to be supported by the company’s Grande Prairie refurbishment facility.

Pricing and Data Center Opportunities Develop

Management reported positive pricing trends in elastic segments such as open camps, turnkey projects and equipment rental, with pricing gains already appearing in bids and contracts. Dexterra is also pursuing workforce accommodation opportunities in Louisiana and West Texas, Canadian data center projects and facilities-management work at an operating U.S. data center.

Near-Term Risks Include Wildfires and Project Timing

Wildfire support activity was roughly half, or slightly less than, a typical year and well below the company’s nominal CAD 25 million target. Installation and demobilization revenue declined CAD 10 million year over year because of project timing, while nation-building awards remain dependent on planning, regulatory reviews and client procurement decisions.

Management Notes Further Uncertainty

Dexterra expects PVC to be largely cash-flow neutral in the near term as it funds software modernization and builds its U.S. operating structure. Management also said the scale of future data center services remains unclear, while wildfire activity in 2027 could range from below normal to materially higher, making the outlook for those activities variable.

Forward Guidance Points to Continued Expansion

Management expects Support Services adjusted EBITDA margins to remain above 9% over the medium term, while Asset Based Services margins should be toward the upper end of the 30% to 40% range in 2026. Dexterra expects most annual free cash flow in the second half of 2026, conversion above 50%, leverage below 2.5 times, new contracts ramping through the first half of 2027 and more installation activity during 2027.

The call presented Dexterra as a growing, cash-generative company with improving margins, stronger returns and a healthier balance sheet. While wildfire volatility and the timing of major projects remain risks, management’s expanding fleet, broad pipeline and U.S. platform provide several avenues for future growth.
